source: Seeded from history/y4 lesson 13 (1066 claimant cards (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 13: 1066: who should be king?. To understand why there was a struggle for the English crown in 1066

cards:
succession
who comes next to rule

claimant
a person who says they should
be king

Witan
the council of important men
who advised the king

Normans
people from Normandy in France

heir
the person who will be the
next ruler
blocks.task: use them to test yourself or a partner.

questions.q: Why did William think he should be king?
questions.a: Edward had promised him, and Harold swore an oath to support him
questions.model: Find William in the table. Reason 1: Edward's promise. Reason 2: Harold's oath. So William felt cheated.

questions.a: The council that advised the king and chose Harold

questions.q: Fill in a claimant card for each of the three: who, where from, reason, strength, weakness.
questions.model: Teacher fills in Harold's card first.

questions.q: Rank the claims from strongest to weakest with a reason.
questions.a: Any ranking with reasons, for example Harold first because the Witan chose him

questions.q: Why did a promise matter so much in 1066?
questions.a: People believed oaths were sacred; breaking one was seen as very wrong

questions.q: Big question: who had the best right to be king?
questions.a: A reasoned view about one claimant using their reason and its weakness
